gate_summary: the inventory is closed over 6 published matching settings; 1 score-affecting values come from the authoritative sample and 2 are delivered runtime defaults nobody has read yet

pending_actions.what_is_missing: a value with an upstream provenance for 2 score-affecting matching settings: FingersMaximalRotation, MatchingScenario. no licence has been activated from this project and nothing has been executed, so no qualification record exists. The SDK's own ReadMe defines installation as extracting the archive and then activating the licensing software; the second step starts a 30-day trial bound to one machine, and that is the maintainer's decision rather than a preflight's (spec section 32)
pending_actions.what_to_do: Everything checkable is in place: the artifacts verify and a Java toolchain is available. Run `make stage11a-qualify`. It will ask the SDK for the FingerExtractor and FingerMatcher licences and stop with TRIAL_LICENCE_NOT_ACTIVATED if the 30-day trial has not been activated — the licence is the one precondition that cannot be checked without loading the SDK, so the harness asks it rather than predicting it. The run scores only synthetic fixtures and never SD300.
pending_actions.what_it_would_answer: Each of these changes the score, and the pinned manual states a default for none of them — while stating defaults for the face-side settings in the same tables, so the absence is a property of the document rather than of the reading. One constructed engine reports all of them, and each becomes a DELIVERED_RUNTIME_DEFAULT: an upstream authority, recorded rather than chosen.

scope: this document counts only the settings of this gate; the other profile gate counts its own, and no number here spans both

published_settings.published_meaning: Low (slower but more accurate), Medium, or High (faster but less accurate)
the maximal rotation of the fingerprint
NotUsed, LatentFinger, FingerFastMatcherLicense, or Minex for MINEX-compliant ISO template matching
whether the results include the per-record details
the maximum number of returned matching results
whether matching stops at the first positive result

authoritative_sample: Tutorials/Biometrics/Java/verify-finger — upstream's own complete 1:1 verification program, the only sample in the archive that performs the whole route this benchmark needs
why_one_sample_only: Upstream ships many tutorials and they configure the engine differently: the enrolment tutorial sets a template size the verification tutorial never touches, and the verification tutorial sets a matching speed the enrolment tutorial never touches. A profile taking one value from each would be a configuration no upstream program has ever run, so only the complete 1:1 program counts (docs/adr/0105).

observations.subject: which matching settings are externally selectable
observations.statement: The biometric engine publishes FingersMatchingSpeed, FingersMaximalRotation, MatchingThreshold, MatchingScenario, MatchingWithDetails, MatchingFirstResultOnly and MatchingMaximalResultCount.

observations.subject: the preset family and what upstream says it costs
observations.statement: NMatchingSpeed publishes Low = 0, Medium = 128 and High = 256, documented as 'Low matching speed (slower but more accurate)' and 'High matching speed (faster but less accurate)'. The manual adds that the slow matcher offers low and medium and the fast matcher offers all three.

observations.subject: which preset upstream's own 1:1 code selects
observations.statement: The verify-finger tutorial calls setFingersMatchingSpeed(NMatchingSpeed.LOW) before verifying. It is an explicit choice in upstream's own working 1:1 example, not a value fpbench picked.

observations.subject: how a single score is arrived at
observations.statement: The manual states that matching is performed at the record level and the resulting scores are fused into a single similarity score, with the intermediate scores available through NMatchingDetails.
